date_note: The Tribune (PTI) says police spoke 'on Thursday' (26 November); no raid date is stated on the pages read.
exec: Delhi Police say they rescued 164 foreign nationals from a Noida call centre where, according to police, people were forced into investment-scam work.
plain: Delhi Police say they rescued 164 foreign nationals, 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from a Noida call centre. Police allege they were lured with job offers and made to run fake investment scams. One Malaysian has been arrested.

sources.name: The Tribune (PTI): Lured with job offers, forced into cyber fraud: 164 foreigners rescued in Noida raid
Nile Post (Agencies): India busts cyberfraud and trafficking network rescuing 164 foreigners

evidence.quote: the Crime Branch of Delhi Police has rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians

summary: Delhi Police Crime Branch rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from a Noida call centre, according to the PTI report in The Tribune. Police allege the recruits were lured with job offers, had their passports taken and were made to run fake investment scams. One Malaysian national has been arrested; police are investigating a wider network.
title: Delhi Police rescue 164 foreign nationals from Noida call centre in alleged cyber-fraud and trafficking case

validation.note: The Tribune (PTI) and Nile Post (Agencies) each state the 164 rescued and the arrest, citing police; no police release read. BBC and Straits Times pages could not be loaded.
